# ADR: Embed the coding conventions in the root AGENTS.md, regenerated by one command

## Status
Accepted

## Area
setup

## Decided by
An agent in an unattended run, with no review

## Context

This repository's own context file, the root `AGENTS.md` (which `CLAUDE.md` links to), carries the coding conventions as its "Coding Conventions" section. Agents working here, including cloud sessions that cannot read the owner's `~/.agents`, get them only through that file, so the section is a copy of `setup/CODING_CONVENTIONS.md` with every heading demoted one level, and the structure check fails when the two differ.

The weekly sync of `setup/CODING_CONVENTIONS.md` from the owner's dotfiles therefore needs a second edit every time the conventions change. Nothing made that edit, and CI did not run the structure check: https://github.com/doodledood/pi-plugins/pull/82 merged a new conventions file with the embedded section stale, and main stayed red until a hand-made follow-up, https://github.com/doodledood/pi-plugins/pull/83.

## Decision

Keep the conventions embedded, and make the copy mechanical. `embedConventions` in `scripts/verify-structure-helpers.mjs` is the one transform: it replaces only the "## Coding Conventions" section (to the next `## ` heading or the end of the file), demotes headings outside fenced code blocks, and throws when the section is missing. The structure check compares the file against that transform's output, and its failure names `node scripts/embed-conventions.mjs`, which writes it (`--check` only reports). A pull-request workflow runs the structure check, so a stale section cannot merge green.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Replace the section with a pointer to `setup/CODING_CONVENTIONS.md`.** Rejected: an agent that reads the context file is not guaranteed to follow a pointer, and the conventions are the part of that file every change is held to.
- **Keep the check and edit the section by hand.** Rejected: that is the step the sync kept missing, and a hand-made copy is where drift starts.
- **Run the check in CI only, with no command.** Rejected: the failure would still need a hand edit to fix.

## Consequences

### Positive

- A conventions sync is the copy plus one command, and a drifted section fails the pull request rather than main.
- The check and the fix share one transform, so they cannot disagree.

### Negative

- The root `AGENTS.md` holds a generated section that must not be edited by hand; the structure check is what says so.

## Enforced by
`embedConventions` and `validateEmbeddedConventions` in `scripts/verify-structure-helpers.mjs` (run by `scripts/verify-structure.mjs`), `scripts/embed-conventions.mjs`, and `.github/workflows/structure-check.yml`, which runs the structure check on every pull request to `main`.
